card.name: Subject before 'are given together'
card.fires_on: The subject word (drugs, they, these agents) or the verb 'are' right after 'when' or 'if' in a drug-interaction sentence. The next words are about the drugs being used or given together.

modes.label: Drug noun after when/if these
modes.description: The noun 'drugs' or 'agents' after 'when the' or 'when these', just before 'are used concomitantly'.
modes.example: It may be necessary to decrease the dose of verapamil and/or the dose of the neuromuscular blocking agent when the<< drugs>> are used concomitantly.

modes.label: The verb 'are' before co-administration
modes.description: The verb 'are' after 'they', 'these drugs' or 'these agents', just before 'given', 'administered' or 'co-administered'.
modes.example: phenytoin and barbiturate blood levels should be monitored more frequently if these drugs<< are>> given concurrently.

card.writes: It pushes the model toward words about drugs being combined or taken together, and away from partnership or combination words.
card.plain: It marks the spot in an interaction warning where the text is about to say the drugs are given together.
